videos.script: Installing a system takes an hour. Copying a finished one takes seconds. So the obvious way to get ten lab machines is to build one well and copy it. {{copy}} The copy is called a clone, and it has a catch. A computer keeps its identity on its own disk: its name, a unique ID, the keys that prove it is itself. A plain copy carries all of it. {{catch}} You will make a clone and watch it come up with the wrong name and no network at all. Then you will do it properly. Strip the identity out of the original, which is called sealing it, and keep it as a template. {{seal}} Every machine made from the template gets a fresh identity on its first boot. And because each one is a thin layer on the template, making one costs almost no disk at all. {{template}}
